text:
marta: quick sync — deciding between in-VPC read cache agent vs required PrivateLink for tenant control-plane reads (certs, metadata, flags). who wants which tradeoffs?

devin: short answer: cache gives big p99 wins and slashes egress for busy tenants. invalidation is the hard part.

kai: agree. propose outbound-only mTLS pubsub (no inbound peering). framed protobuf messages, seq nums, per-tenant watermark. lightweight and firewall-friendly.

marta: requirements: some customers want revocations <=10s. is that realistic with a cache?

devin: yes if we treat certain invalidations as "priority" and require synchronous verification on receipt. flow: publish priority invalidation -> agent receives -> agent blocks local responses for that key until it pulls authoritative state. effectively strong revoke.

kai: also add a global "tombstone/kill-switch" topic. if CP publishes tenant tombstone, agents must immediately deny and enter fallback. useful for compromise response.

ops-bot: infra-ticket created NTW-523 for outbound-pubsub-agent prototype; owners <@marta> <@devin>.

marta: audit trail question: do we stream every agent decision back to CP in realtime, or batch signed digests? compliance teams push realtime for some tenants.

devin: realtime increases egress. compromise: opt-in realtime-audit flag per tenant. default = 1min batched signed digest. signed assertions make post-hoc forensics possible.

kai: key management: two modes: 1) CP-provisioned short-lived signing keys (bootstrapped once via PrivateLink), 2) BYOK/KMS where customer keeps keys and agent signs locally. BYOK required for some regs.

marta: bootstrap flow sketch:
```text
1) customer provisions PrivateLink endpoint + grants bootstrap role
2) agent uses PrivateLink once to exchange bootstrap certs/credentials
3) agent opens persistent outbound mTLS to CP pubsub with cert
4) CP sends initial snapshot + tenant subscription
```

devin: heartbeats should include last_applied_seq. if agent misses 2 heartbeats, CP marks agent stale and publishes tombstone to force revalidation and alerting.

kai: metrics we must collect: cache_hit_ratio, avg_staleness_ms, invalidation_latency_ms (publish->apply), outbound_egress_bytes, audit_egress_bytes, bootstrap_success_rate, tombstone_count.

marta: fallback semantics: default: if invalidation channel fails and PrivateLink available -> sync pull. if neither available -> fail_closed for HIGH-sensitivity ops, fail_open (with warn) for LOW-sensitivity. needs per-operation sensitivity label.

security-bot: security note: client cert rotate frequently (<12h) for pubsub link; short lifetimes reduce key exposure. also restrict pubsub topics per-tenant with RBAC.

devin: pseudocode for request handling:
```text
if op.sensitivity == HIGH:
  if cache.hit and not expired: return cached
  elif invalidation_channel.ok: sync_pull_and_update; if fresh: return; else: 403
  else: 403
else:
  try cache, then invalidation sync, then private_endpoint call, then 403
```

kai: operational notes: helm-deployed daemonset + sidecar for auto-update of minors. major upgrades opt-in. observable hooks for sequence numbers and tombstones.

marta: decision (tentative): implement opt-in cache agent with outbound-only mTLS pubsub invalidations, single-bootstrap PrivateLink step, BYOK support for regulated tenants, realtime audit optional. rollout: 3 pilot tenants, 30d metrics collection (staleness/egress), runbook for tombstone & failed-invalidation.

ops-bot: updated NTW-523 with checklist: prototype, runbook, metrics dashboard, legal review for BYOK.

marta: I'll write an RFC follow-up with sequence diagrams and the exact sensitivity labels. post any missing items here. thanks! :raised_hands:
